keyFindings.description: Round 3, finding 1: one refused call can increment one breaker key twice, so the unreviewed pass arrives after a single refusal. Breaker.revised loops over the refused array and increments per element, while askIdentity keys a block ask on its opening, the first 60 normalized code points. Two distinct blocks in one write whose text starts alike collapse to one key. Measured at this head with newAsks on a doc-edit inserting #first and #second carrying the same question: two asks, two ids, one distinct identity. One refusal of that call therefore sets the count to 2, revised returns tripsNext so the agent is told "This is the second refusal of this call on its target" on what is its first, and the next send trips: outcome "breaker", no rules call, no charter call, both asks posted unjudged. That is round 2's finding 3(a) re-entering through multiplicity rather than through the two registers, and both callers can produce duplicates (the rules path maps matches to identities, the charter path maps every ask of the call). Remedy: deduplicate at the breaker's boundary, revised taking a set of the things it is handed, with a regression refusing one call carrying two same-opening blocks and asserting the second send is still refused and only the third passes. Keying a block ask on its id as well as its opening would also close the Q3 minor (two different asks sharing 60 opening characters share a breaker identity) and keeps the termination the opening gives, since a resend of a block carries both.

Round 3, finding 2: the unjudged path has never executed outside a fake, and the premise that it cannot is wrong. The code is right and I checked every link — runRulesCheck answers unjudged with asksPartial and no model call only when the read failed and the filter emptied the list; the entry carries ruleOutcome and ruleAsksPartial; decision-record selects it on a non-null ruleOutcome; askgate-report counts it in calls, partial and its own unjudged line; settleRules neither resets nor advances the halt count. But no live record in three rounds carries ruleAsksPartial true, let alone ruleOutcome unjudged, and the reader's 0 proves the line prints, not that a real record reaches it. The stated reason is that Dispatch answered every de-duplication read so no run could make one fail. A run can: readDocumentBlocks resolves an upload's document by its --name and artifactByReference throws a plain Error, not DocumentNotFoundError, when two documents answer to one filename (packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-execute.ts:1423-1424), so readDocument catches it and answers failed; and a second upload of one name makes a second document rather than a version, which this change's own decision record relies on. The recipe is three commands on a scratch issue: dispatch artifact --name probe.md twice, then a third upload of that name whose markdown carries only ask blocks with ids. This is the one path whose whole purpose is to leave a trace when nobody judged an ask — the remedy for round 2's silent pass — so unit evidence is the weakest place to stop, and the repository's rule is that a missing surface is a blocker only when no surface can reach it.

The README still says the request caps the list of asks at 32 KiB, while the code's own comment now says a call of more than roughly 111 asks passes that bound at the per-ask floor. Measured at this head: 300 asks of about 1 KB render 51,383 bytes, and both thermonuclear agents measured the same shape (111 asks at 32,858 bytes, 128 at 37,907, 200 at 34,181, 256 at 75,923). The floor is the right trade — round 2 rejected dropping asks, and every ask is still listed with both its ends — so the sentence should say what the code says rather than the floor changing. Fold it into the same push as finding 1.

The architect's Q3 minor, judged: askIdentity keys a non-retype ask on its opening, so two different asks sharing their first 60 code points share a breaker identity, and after two refusals of one the other is passed unreviewed. It is not a hole to block on. Sameness by opening is what makes the breaker terminate — a full-text identity would let an agent that rewords its tail loop for ever — and every pass is recorded as outcome breaker and announced to the agent. Fast-follow, or closed for free by including a block's id in its identity as finding 1's remedy suggests.

The architect's other Q3 minor, judged: askgate-report.ts still accepts --sessions '' where --dispatch-project '' is refused by name; it fails later on the missing --sample with exit 2 and nothing on stdout. It fails closed and can let no ask through unjudged. Fast-follow.

notes: CI read on GitHub at the code head cff21b26fe3865de128dcf0d4df30ad3f8fa4424: main's rulesets require lint, typecheck, test and pr-title; lint, typecheck and pr-title are completed and success, and test and the non-required pi-envoy lane were still in progress at the read. The compare from that commit to the reviewed head lists only .legion/ paths. The round is a request for changes, which stands whatever CI says; a later approval must read the settled required set, and the A1 pin runs inside test and pi-envoy.

A1's pin, which the architect asked me to read because describeAsks changed: the four MEASURED constants in askgate.test.ts:3963-3968 are untouched by this round's three commits (the diff holds no MEASURED or hash line), and the pin test passes here — 343 tests across the askgate files, 1 skip, 0 fail, with both thermonuclear agents running it in isolation (1 pass each). The rendered-request constant is MEASURED["the rendered request"], 48e8ef9c…, and its fixed input is one small ask that is neither clipped nor id-bounded, which is why a renderer change leaves it byte-identical. That is what A1 pins and it holds; it also means the pin exercises neither the middle clip nor the id bound, which the round's own tests cover instead.

Round 2's four findings: findings 1 (the head-only clip) and 4 (the unbounded id) are closed, verified by re-running my own probes at this head — the recommendation now survives every shape that lost it (1/1, 2/2, 10/10, 30/30, 120/120 against 0/1, 0/2, 0/30 before), and an id of 3, 32,000, 64,000 or 200,000 characters all leave the list at 402 to 527 bytes with the other ask's text whole. clipMiddle is sound at both cut points: a sweep over escaped text holding entities and multi-byte characters at budgets 0 to 128 produced no U+FFFD, no bare <, and no half-written entity, and the bound holds from 40 bytes up. Finding 3 (the breaker) is closed in both reported cases and left finding 1 above. Finding 2 (the upload judged by nobody) is closed in code and left the evidence gap above. Threads PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-tYF and PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_S8b are accepted and left resolved; PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-tYH and PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v-tYJ carry my answer and were unresolved.

Both thermonuclear agents ran at the reviewed head and returned CHANGES. Both found finding 1 independently and I reproduced it myself before writing it. Both also raised the 32 KiB overflow, which I judged a documented trade rather than a defect: the code states it, the consequence is a larger request rather than an ask nobody judged, and it needs a single write of more than a hundred new ask blocks; what I took from it is the README sentence above. Their remaining items (batching the request, a clipMiddle contract below 28 bytes that no caller can reach) are not findings.

The merge of main at cff21b26 brought no product change: its own diff holds three changelog conflict resolutions and no source resolution, and the deep agent's restriction of 9bdbb4a6..cff21b26 to the AskGate files, the report and the README is empty. The tester re-ran every live case at the merge head rather than relying on that.
